description: Chinese / math punctuation — spacing rules, two-cell symbols, sentence-final punctuation.

zh_punct.description: Chinese punctuation (jieba segmentation, one blank cell between words)

cases.note: Chinese ？ is two cells ⠐⠄ with no trailing blank (two-cell sentence-final mark, like 。 ！)
dunhao 、 separator between items (蕉=jiao1: iao final is ⠜)
Chinese semicolon ⠰ (56) — the ASCII ; is the ⠆ (23) one
two chars + Chinese ？ (⠐⠄, no trailing blank)
regression for ？ bug: Chinese ？ must produce ⠐⠄, not the English ⠦

punct_adjacent.description: Two marks in a row — an auto-space belongs between a word and the next word, not between a word and the mark that closes it

cases.note: ）'s space_after does not survive the 。 that follows it: 。 carries no space_before, which in this table says it is written against what precedes it. The blank before （ is that mark's own space_before, and stays.
same at a closing quote: ”⠘⠘ then 。⠐⠆ with nothing between them

the other direction: ：asks for a blank after and “ for one before — two rules, one blank. An opening mark keeps it, so the veto above is about what the next mark declares, not about marks being adjacent.
